properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 1 at 6:46AM CDT until October 2 at 10:00PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Austin/San Antonio has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Devils River At Pafford Crossing near Comstock affecting Val Verde
County.

...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Texas...

Devils River At Bakers Crossing 19N Of Comstock affecting Val Verde
County.

Devils River At Cauthorn Ranch Near Juno affecting Val Verde
County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Devils River at Pafford Crossing nr Comstock.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 5.0 feet, (1.5 meters), Minor lowland flooding one
quarter mile wide at Pafford Crossing covers most of the right
bank. Turbulent flow above Pafford Crossing to Amistad Reservoir
can wash campers, automobiles, and equipment downstream. At 6.0
feet, (1.8 meters), Moderate lowland flooding over 1/4 mile wide
covers the right bank to the canyon walls. The turbulent flow can
wash motorists, campers, and equipment downstream from Pafford
Crossing to Amistad Reservoir. Livestock are cut off and
potentially drowned below Juno to Amistad Reservoir.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:15 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon to a crest of 6.0 feet late this afternoon. It will
then fall below flood stage late tomorrow morning.
- Flood stage is 5.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 700 PM CDT.

properties.headline: Tropical Storm Warning issued October 1 at 9:22PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...TROPICAL STORM CHOI-WAN MOVING WEST INTO THE NORTHERN
MARIANAS, SOUTHEAST OF ALAMAGAN...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions
for people on Saipan, Tinian, Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan in the
Commonwealth of the Northern Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Tinian, Saipan, and
adjacent coastal waters.

A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Alamagan, Pagan,
and Agrihan in the CNMI.

A Typhoon Watch remains in effect for Alamagan, Pagan, and Agrihan
in the CNMI.

A Typhoon Watch means that typhoon conditions, including winds of 74
mph or more, are possible within 48 hours.
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected within 24 hours.

A Flood Watch remains in effect for Tinian and Saipan. Please listen
closely for any Flash Flood Warnings that might be in effect for
your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 7 PM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W) was
located near latitude 17.0N, longitude 146.4E. This was about 55
miles southeast of Alamagan, 90 miles south-southeast of Pagan,
and 260 miles north-northeast of Guam. Storm motion was west, 280
degrees, at 13 mph. Storm intensity was 45 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Tropical Storm Choi-Wan is expected to slow slightly as it
continues westward overnight, with the center passing to the south
of Alamagan early Friday morning. It is then expected to make a
turn toward the northwest, then north with a decrease in forward
speed through Friday. Then, Choi-wan looks to gradually turn to
the north-northeast on Saturday after it emerges west of the
northern islands. Choi-wan is forecast to intensify through
Friday, potentially becoming a typhoon late Friday night or early
Saturday morning.

This forecasted passage moving along the axis of the far northern
Marianas is still expected to prolong the duration of damaging
winds across the northern islands, likely leading to a lengthy
period of time of damaging to destructive tropical storm
conditions continuing into Sunday afternoon. As Choi-wan is
forecast to strengthen to a typhoon, there is a possibility for
typhoon-force conditions to develop somewhere along the far
northern Marianas. As such, a Typhoon Watch and Tropical Storm
Warning remain in effect for Alamagan, Pagan, and Agrihan. The
latest forecast track has shifted Choi-Wan farther west of the
islands, slightly decreasing this possibility.
properties.instruction:
Stay indoors during heavy rain and tropical storm-force wind
conditions associated with Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W). Heed the
advice of your local emergency managers and officials, and
continue to monitor forecasts by the National Weather Service
office in Tiyan, Guam. Remain in sturdy shelter until the all-
clear is given.

Preparations for Tropical Storm Choi-wan should be complete, or
rapidly rushed to completion. Take small loose object indoors.
Remain in suitable shelter. If no concrete shelter is available,
look for a cave or something similar. Shelter in place until the
all-clear is given.

.WIND INFORMATION...
North to northeast winds of 15 to 25 mph will turn toward the
southeast and increase through Friday as Choi-wan moves west
across the northern CNMI and strengthens, potentially becoming a
typhoon Friday night to the west of Alamagan and Pagan as it turns
to the north. Tropical storm force winds of 39 to 50 mph look to
continue through Sunday. Depending on the track and intensity,
winds may increase to strong tropical storm-force of 58 to 65 mph
early Saturday morning. Typhoon force winds greater than 74 mph
look to remain possible during closest passage.

.COASTAL INUNDATION AND SURF INFORMATION...
Surf will initially build to 8 to 12 feet along east-facing reefs
through Friday morning, then spread along north and west-facing
reefs as the center moves north-northeast west of the northern
CNMI Friday night through Saturday night, increasing by several
feet during this time. As Choi-wan continues to strengthen, surf
will continue to increase, likely becoming dangerous by early next
week. Significant coastal erosion and some coastal inundation is
expected during Choi-wan's passage.

.OTHER STORM EFFECTS...
Periods of rain, widespread heavy showers and scattered thunderstorms
could produce rainfall totals of 10 to 16 inches by early Monday
morning, with up to 20 inches of rainfall possible near the center of
the system.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 1 at 12:15PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
The latest forecasts from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) and
numerical guidance continues to strengthen Tropical Storm Choi-Wan
(26W) as it crosses the Marianas sometime this weekend, possibly
stalling or slowing to a crawl as it does so, becoming a typhoon by
the end of the weekend. Choi-Wan is then forecast to turn north and
accelerate somewhat during the early to middle portion of next week
while it continues strengthening, possibly into a major typhoon.

As all of this occurs, the west to southwest monsoon flow already
encompassing northern Palau (mainly near Koror) and western Yap State
will continue strengthening, with sustained winds of 15 to 20 knots
possible. Strong moisture pooling near the trough axis combined with
at least decent surface convergence should foster increasing shower
and thunderstorm coverage and intensity as we head into the weekend
and early next week. Current indications are for 3 to 6 inches of
rainfall, locally in excess of 8 inches being probable for northern
Palau and western Yap State. This could lead to some minor flooding
concerns and landslide potential, especially near Koror where the
steeper terrain is juxtaposed with the strong moisture pooling and
surface convergence.

As the winds increase, and Choi-Wan strengthens, seas and surf will
also increase. This could lead to hazardous conditions for the
northern reefs and potentially for small craft traversing the waters.

Residents across northern Palau and western Yap States are encouraged
to continue to follow forecast trends at www.weather.gov/gum and on
social media.
